steps.heading: Long data, wide grid
steps.body: pivot_table(values=, index=, columns=, aggfunc=) reshapes tall data into a grid: one row per index value, one column per columns value, aggregated with aggfunc wherever more than one row lands in the same cell.

steps.heading: Revenue by region and category
steps.output:
# category  Bags  Shoes
# region
# East        60    165
# West       125    120
steps.caption: The default aggfunc is 'mean', not 'sum' — always set it explicitly if you want totals.

steps.heading: Related tools
steps.body: crosstab() is a shortcut for pure frequency counts between two columns. stack()/unstack() move column labels into (or out of) the row index, converting between wide and long shapes without re-aggregating.

steps.heading: Filling in the gaps
steps.code: pd.pivot_table(df, values='revenue', index='region', columns='category', aggfunc='sum', fill_value=0)
steps.output: # a region/category combo with no rows shows 0 instead of NaN
steps.caption: You'll practice fill_value, margins, multiple values/aggfuncs, crosstab, and stack/unstack in the cards that follow.
